attributes.nuance_translation: A word that describes the way that others are acting, or may be feeling.

attributes.body:
がる is a う-Verb that is primarily used as a suffix in Japanese. When used in this way, it means 'to act like (A)', or 'to show signs of being (A)', where (A) is the word that it is attached to.

To use がる, you will need to link it to the stem form of an い-Adjective (simply remove the い), or to the stem form of a な-Adjective (do not include the な).

がる is a verb which means 'to give the impression of (A)', or 'to act like (A)'. This is very important in Japanese, as you would not usually say how somebody else feels, unless they told you directly and you are simply repeating what you heard (in which case you would use the quotation particle と).

When you want to express the way you 'think' that someone else feels, but don't have any direct information about it, that is when がる would be natural to use. For example, if you see someone shivering in the cold, you would say something like the following.

The main difference between がる, and がっている, is that がる will be used when a person usually/always acts a certain way, whereas がっている is more about the way someone/something is acting in any specific moment.

Caution

がる may also be used to describe yourself (in the third person). This is when you want to express the way you think that you act/are acting, or a way you assume other people view your behavior.

Fun Fact

The use of がっている to express an 'in the moment' way that someone is acting, is slowly becoming less and less common in modern Japanese. Regularly, そう will be used instead, to express that someone (or something) 'seems' a certain way.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: がる attaches to adjectives to describe the observed feelings or desires of another person, e.g. 寒がる 'seems cold', ほしがる 'seems to want (A)', and so on. When combined with the たい-form of verbs, it becomes たがる, expressing observed desire, e.g. 飲みたがる 'seems to want to drink'.

first_relatable.title: がる
first_relatable.meaning: To feel, To think, To act as if, To want, To desire

attributes.body: The たい form expresses personal desires, like バナナが食べたい ('I want to eat a banana'). がる, on the other hand, is used to show that someone else seems to want something, like 食べたがっている ('[He/she] seems like they want to eat'). The たい form is generally not used for others' desires unless the subject has explicitly made their desire clear.

second_relatable.title: がる
second_relatable.meaning: To feel, To think, To act as if, To want, To desire

attributes.body: がほしい and がる both express desire but differ in usage. がほしい straightforwardly expresses the speaker's own wants, e.g. 車がほしい ('I want a car.'). In contrast, がる attaches to adjectives (e.g. ほしい becomes ほしがる) to describe what someone else appears to feel, e.g. 田中さんは車をほしがっている ('Mr. Tanaka seems to want a car.').

attributes.body: てほしい and がる both relate to expressing desire but are used differently. てほしい is used when you want someone to do something, e.g. これを買ってほしい ('I want you to buy this.'). がる describes what another person appears to feel, e.g. 田中さんは車を買いたがっている ('Mr. Tanaka seems to want to buy a car.').
